nodes.name: 2K Games
nodes.summary: Novato, CA-based publishing label of orgs/Take-Two Interactive. Established 2005. Home to major franchises including NBA 2K, Borderlands, Civilization, XCOM, WWE 2K, and BioShock. Multiple development studios under the 2K umbrella.

nodes.name: 4A Games
nodes.ownership: Subsidiary of Embracer Group (via Saber Interactive, 2020-2024; retained by Embracer after Saber sale)
nodes.summary: Ukrainian-Maltese video game developer based in Sliema, Malta with a studio in Kyiv, Ukraine. Best known for the Metro series (Metro 2033, Metro: Last Light, Metro Exodus). Founded in 2006 by former GSC Game World developers who worked on S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl.

nodes.ownership: Acquired by [[orgs/Microsoft Gaming]] for $68.7B, closed Oct 13, 2023

The company was the center of the game industry's largest labor disputes and unionization wave.

nodes.summary: Largest certified union in US video game history at formation (March 2024). Represents 600 (now 400) quality assurance testers across Activision Blizzard studios in California, Texas, and Minnesota. Voluntarily recognized by Microsoft under the 2022 Labor Neutrality Agreement.

nodes.name: Affinity Partners
nodes.summary: US private-equity firm, Miami, FL. Formed 2021 by Jared Kushner (CEO of Affinity; President Trump's son-in-law).

nodes.name: Amazon Games
nodes.summary: The video game division of Amazon, formerly Amazon Game Studios (2012-2020), Amazon Games (2020-2025), now Amazon Games again. Headquarters in Seattle, WA. A division of Amazon Entertainment.

nodes.name: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)
nodes.summary: US venture firm (SF/Palo Alto, CA). One of the most active gaming VCs; maintains a dedicated Games fund (total $1.2B gaming AUM).

nodes.name: Annapurna Interactive
nodes.ownership: Division of Annapurna Pictures (owned by Megan Ellison)
nodes.summary: Award-winning video game publisher under Annapurna Pictures. Known for What Remains of Edith Finch, Stray, Outer Wilds, Neon White, and Cocoon.

nodes.name: Arc System Works
nodes.ownership: Private (independently owned); founded by Minoru Kidooka
nodes.summary: Premier Japanese fighting game developer; creators of Guilty Gear, Dragon Ball FighterZ, and BlazBlue. Headquartered in Shinagawa, Tokyo. Founded in 1988 by Minoru Kidooka. Independently owned. Known for pioneering modern anime fighting game presentation and rollback netcode.

nodes.name: Arkane Studios
nodes.summary: Acclaimed immersive sim developer with two historic studios — only Lyon survives. Founded 1999 in Lyon, France. Opened Austin, Texas studio in 2006. Acquired by ZeniMax Media in 2010. Known for the Dishonored series, Prey, and Deathloop.
wikilinks: events/2024-05-07 — ZeniMax studio closures (Arkane Austin Tango Alpha Dog)

nodes.name: Arrowhead Game Studios
nodes.summary: Swedish video game developer based in Stockholm. Founded in 2008 by a group of students from Luleå University of Technology. Known for cooperative multiplayer games — Magicka, the original Helldivers, and the phenomenally successful Helldivers 2 (2024).

nodes.name: Asmodee
nodes.summary: French board game publisher, one of the largest in the world. Owns major board game IPs including Catan, Ticket to Ride, Dobble/Spot It!, Splendor, and Pandemic. Also operates digital board game adaptations.

nodes.name: Atlus
nodes.ownership: Wholly owned subsidiary of Sega Corporation (via Sega Sammy Holdings)
nodes.summary: Japanese video game developer best known for the Persona and Shin Megami Tensei series. Subsidiary of orgs/Sega Corporation since 2013. Headquartered in Shinagawa, Tokyo.

nodes.summary: - Full name: Avalanche Software - Location: Salt Lake City, Utah - Founded: October 1995 - Founder: John Blackburn (current CEO) - Parent: Warner Bros. Games (since 2017; previously Disney Interactive Studios 2005–2016) - Employees: 400 (estimated, grew significantly for Hogwarts Legacy) - Union status: No union - Website: avalanchesoftware.com

nodes.name: Bandai Namco Entertainment Inc.
nodes.ownership: Wholly owned subsidiary of Bandai Namco Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7832)
nodes.summary: Japanese video game publisher and the digital/game publishing arm of the Bandai Namco Group. Headquartered in Minato, Tokyo. Publishes major franchises: Tekken, Gundam, Soulcalibur, Ace Combat, The Idolmaster, and serves as co-publisher for orgs/FromSoftware titles (Elden Ring, Dark Souls, Armored Core VI).

nodes.name: Beenox
nodes.summary: Canadian game developer based in Quebec City — primary Activision studio for PC porting and Call of Duty support. Founded in 2000, acquired by Activision in 2005. Beenox has been a key support studio for the Call of Duty franchise, handling PC ports and additional development support since 2018.

nodes.name: Behaviour Interactive
nodes.summary: Montreal, QC studio — in-scope (Canada). Developer/publisher of Dead by Daylight (genre-leading online horror). Backed by the Haveli Investments Gaming Fund.

nodes.name: Bend Studio
nodes.summary: Bend Studio is a Bend, Oregon-based game developer and subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment. Best known for Days Gone (2019). The studio has a tumultuous recent history: its Days Gone sequel was rejected, a live-service pivot collapsed, and the resulting layoffs cut 30% of its workforce.

nodes.name: Bethesda Game Studios
nodes.ownership: Subsidiary of ZeniMax Media (Microsoft Gaming / Xbox division)
nodes.summary: Microsoft/Xbox's flagship RPG developer — Rockville, Austin, Dallas, Montreal. Best known for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011), Fallout 4 (2015), and Starfield (2023). Approximately 500 employees across four studios.

nodes.name: Bethesda Softworks
nodes.ownership: Subsidiary of ZeniMax Media (Microsoft Gaming / Xbox division)
nodes.summary: Legacy publisher founded 1986; acquired by Microsoft 2021 as part of ZeniMax Media ($8.1B). HQ Rockville, MD. President Jill Braff. Publishes The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, Starfield, Doom, Wolfenstein, Quake, and Dishonored franchises.

nodes.name: BioWare
nodes.summary: US + Canada studio, owned by orgs/Electronic Arts. Known for Mass Effect, Dragon Age, Star Wars: The Old Republic.

nodes.name: Bitkraft Ventures
nodes.summary: Leading VC firm focused on gaming and emerging technology. Operates six funds (four equity, two crypto) with $1.05B total AUM. Most active VC investor in gaming globally in 2020, 2021, and 2022 per PitchBook.

nodes.name: Blizzard CWA Unions (bargaining coalition)
nodes.region: US (Irvine CA + Austin TX + Boston MA + Albany NY)
nodes.summary: The largest union contract victory in North American video game history. 1,900 workers across 6 Blizzard Entertainment bargaining units won their first collective bargaining agreement in early September 2026.

nodes.name: Blizzard Entertainment
nodes.region: US (Irvine, CA + Austin, TX + Boston, MA + Albany, NY)
nodes.ownership: Subsidiary of Activision Blizzard (holding company), which is owned by [[orgs/Microsoft Gaming]]
nodes.summary: Legendary American game developer and publisher, now the most unionized AAA studio in North America. Founded 1991 as Silicon & Synapse, Blizzard created Warcraft, StarCraft, Diablo, Overwatch, and Hearthstone. Acquired by Activision in the 2008 Vivendi merger, then by Microsoft in 2023 as part of the $68.7B Activision Blizzard acquisition.

nodes.name: Bohemia Interactive
nodes.summary: Czech video game developer and publisher based in Prague. Privately held, founder-owned. Known for military simulation games — the Arma series, Operation Flashpoint, and DayZ.

nodes.name: Bonfire Studios
nodes.summary: Irvine, CA studio — in-scope. Independent video game developer. Founded 2016, 51-200 employees (LinkedIn). a16z portfolio (per a16z investment list, 2026-01-15).

nodes.name: Bungie
nodes.ownership: Subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment (acquired July 2022 for $3.6B)
nodes.summary: Bungie is a Bellevue, WA-based AAA game developer and subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment. Best known for creating the Halo, Destiny, and Marathon franchises. nodes.name: ByteDance (Gaming)
nodes.summary: TikTok parent company's ill-fated gaming ambition — a case study in rapid expansion and collapse. ByteDance entered AAA gaming at scale in 2019, built Nuverse to over 3,000 employees, then abruptly exited in November 2023.

nodes.name: CCP Games
nodes.summary: Icelandic game developer, founded 1997. Best known for EVE Online, the long-running space MMO. Acquired by Korean publisher Pearl Abyss in 2018 for $425M. Approximately 250 employees in Reykjavík and London.

nodes.name: CD Projekt RED
nodes.summary: Polish AAA game developer, the primary development subsidiary of CD Projekt S.A. Known for The Witcher series and Cyberpunk 2077. Approximately 1,250 employees across Warsaw, Kraków, and Wrocław offices.

nodes.name: CD Projekt
nodes.summary: Polish video game company, HQ Warsaw. Developer of The Witcher series and Cyberpunk 2077. One of the few major game companies that did not participate in the 2023-2026 mass layoff wave — headcount grew during this period.

nodes.name: CVC Capital Partners
nodes.summary: Global PE firm, Luxembourg HQ. Active gaming investor with two major US/CA-adjacent deals.

nodes.name: Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPP Investments)
nodes.summary: Canadian sovereign pension (Toronto, ON). In-scope LP. Participated in the Keywords Studios acquisition (led by EQT, with Temasek) — completed 2024-10-24 ($2.8B).

nodes.name: Candivore
nodes.summary: Mobile studio (Tel Aviv). Developer of Match Masters. Backed by the Haveli Investments Gaming Fund.

nodes.name: Capcom USA
nodes.ownership: Wholly owned subsidiary of Capcom Co., Ltd. (Japan)
nodes.summary: American subsidiary of orgs/Capcom Co., Ltd., handling US sales, marketing, localization, and community management. Headquartered in San Francisco, California. Established 1985 as Capcom's first international subsidiary.

nodes.name: Capcom
nodes.region: JP (Osaka HQ + Tokyo) / US (Capcom USA — San Francisco, CA)
nodes.summary: Major Japanese video game publisher and developer. HQ Osaka, Japan. Listed on Tokyo Stock Exchange (TYO: 9697). Known for Resident Evil, Monster Hunter, Street Fighter, Devil May Cry, and Mega Man. CEO Haruhiro Tsujimoto.

nodes.name: Codemasters
nodes.summary: Southam, UK-based racing game developer, owned by orgs/Electronic Arts. One of the longest-running game developers in the UK (founded 1986). Specializes in licensed racing simulations. Acquired by EA in 2021 for $1.2B.

nodes.name: Coffee Stain Studios
nodes.summary: Swedish video game developer, based in Skövde. Best known for Goat Simulator (2014) and Satisfactory (2024, 1.0 release). Founded by six students from the University of Skövde's game development program.

nodes.name: Compulsion Games
nodes.ownership: Independent (spun out from Xbox Game Studios July 2026); formerly subsidiary of Xbox Game Studios (Microsoft Gaming) 2018–2026
nodes.summary: Independent game developer based in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. Founded in 2009 by Guillaume Provost. Acquired by Microsoft in 2018 as part of Xbox Game Studios, Compulsion developed the cult hits Contrast and We Happy Few before creating the critically acclaimed South of Midnight (released April 2025). The studio spun out from Xbox in July 2026 a...

nodes.name: Creative Assembly Ltd
nodes.ownership: Wholly owned subsidiary of Sega Corporation (JP)
nodes.summary: UK-based video game developer, wholly owned by Sega Corporation. Best known for the Total War strategy series and Alien: Isolation. The studio suffered extensively in Sega's European restructuring following the cancellation of its live-service extraction shooter Hyenas in September 2023.

events/2024-03-28 — Sega 240 European layoffs + Relic sale

nodes.name: Criterion Games
nodes.summary: Guildford, UK-based studio, owned by orgs/Electronic Arts. Historically known for the Burnout and Need for Speed franchises. Since 2022 has primarily supported the Battlefield franchise.

nodes.name: Crytek GmbH
nodes.region: DE (Frankfurt, Germany; with offices in Kyiv, Istanbul)
nodes.ownership: Private (founded by the Yerli brothers: Avni, Cevat, and Faruk Yerli)
nodes.summary: German video game developer and game engine creator, headquartered in Frankfurt. Privately held by the Yerli brothers. Known for the Crysis series (famous for pushing PC hardware benchmarks), Hunt: Showdown extraction shooter, and the CRYENGINE middleware platform.
wikilinks: events/2025-02-12 — Crytek 60 layoffs + Crysis 4 on hold

nodes.name: CyberConnect2
nodes.ownership: Independent (went independent in 2021 after majority stake buyback)
nodes.summary: Japanese video game developer; creators of the .hack// series and Naruto: Ultimate Ninja Storm franchise. Headquartered in Fukuoka, Japan. Founded 1996 by Hiroshi Matsuyama. Known for anime-licensed games and original IP.

nodes.name: DECA Games
nodes.summary: Berlin-based mobile game developer and publisher, acquired by Embracer Group in 2021. Specializes in mobile free-to-play games and live operations. Part of Embracer's mobile gaming portfolio alongside Easybrain and CrazyLabs.

nodes.name: DICE (EA Digital Illusions CE)
nodes.summary: Stockholm-based studio, owned by orgs/Electronic Arts. Flagship developer of the Battlefield series. Founded 1992, acquired by EA in 2006.

nodes.name: Dark Horse Media
nodes.summary: American comic book and game publishing company founded in 1986 by Mike Richardson. Best known for Dark Horse Comics, one of the largest independent comic publishers in the US. Also operates Dark Horse Games, a video game development/publishing division.

nodes.name: Demonware
nodes.summary: Activision's online services and netcode engineering studio, based in Dublin and Shanghai. Founded in 2003, acquired by Activision in 2007. Demonware manages the online infrastructure for the Call of Duty franchise including matchmaking, data services, and anti-cheat systems.

nodes.name: Devolver Digital
nodes.summary: Indie game publisher known for a distinctive, irreverent brand. Portfolio includes Hotline Miami, Enter the Gungeon, Cult of the Lamb, The Stanley Parable, and Trek to Yomi.

nodes.name: Double Fine Productions
nodes.ownership: Subsidiary of Xbox Game Studios (Microsoft Gaming)
nodes.summary: American video game developer based in San Francisco, California. Founded in 2000 by legendary game designer Tim Schafer. Known for creative, character-driven games including Psychonauts, Brütal Legend, and Broken Age. Acquired by Microsoft in 2019.

nodes.name: Dream Games
nodes.summary: Mobile studio (Istanbul + US/CA presence), maker of Royal Match. CVC Capital Partners agreed (2025-05) to acquire a majority stake ($5B EV) — a $2.5B capital injection (per Reuters/CorpDev, to be archived).

nodes.name: EA Sports
nodes.region: US (Orlando FL, Seattle WA, Vancouver CA, other)
nodes.summary: US studio group, owned by orgs/Electronic Arts. Multiple studios (Orlando FL, Seattle WA, Vancouver CA, and others). Known for EA Sports FC, Madden NFL, NBA Live, NHL, F1, UFC.

nodes.name: EQT
nodes.summary: Global PE firm (Sweden HQ). Led the $2.8B acquisition of Keywords Studios (closed 2024-10-24), a global gaming services provider.

nodes.name: ESL FACEIT Group
nodes.summary: Esports organizer (world's #1). Part of PIF's Savvy Games Group (acquired 2022). US/CA presence via tournament ops.

nodes.name: Easybrain
nodes.summary: Cyprus-based mobile game developer known for Sudoku.com and other puzzle games. One of Embracer Group's largest mobile gaming subsidiaries.

nodes.name: Electronic Arts (EA)
nodes.ownership: PE-owned (post-close: Silver Lake + PIF + Affinity; was public)
nodes.summary: US games publisher, HQ Redwood City, CA. Founded 1982 by Trip Hawkins. Anchor node of the power map: subject of the largest leveraged buyout in history (agreed 2025-09-29, $52.5B, expected to close Q1 2027).
wikilinks: orgs/Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia

nodes.summary: Embracer Group AB (formerly THQ Nordic AB, formerly Nordic Games Licensing AB) is a Swedish video game and media holding company headquartered in Karlstad, Sweden. nodes.name: Epic Games
nodes.summary: US game publisher, Unreal Engine developer, and Fortnite creator. Headquarters: Cary, North Carolina. Privately held, controlled by CEO Tim Sweeney. Post-money valuation of $31.5B as of April 2022 (sources/2023-09-28 — variety-epic-830-layoffs-bandcamp).
wikilinks: events/2022-04-29 — NLRB complaint Epic hiring discrimination

nodes.name: Firaxis Games
nodes.summary: Baltimore, MD-based studio, owned by orgs/2K Games / orgs/Take-Two Interactive. Founded 1996 by Sid Meier. Developer of the Civilization (turn-based 4X strategy) and XCOM (turn-based tactical) series. Known for long development cycles and post-launch content support.

nodes.name: Firesprite
nodes.summary: Firesprite is a Liverpool, UK-based game developer and subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment. Formed by former Sony Studio Liverpool (Wipeout) staff after that studio's 2012 closure. Best known for Horizon Call of the Mountain (PSVR2).

nodes.name: Fishlabs
nodes.summary: German video game developer based in Hamburg. Best known for the Galaxy on Fire series of space combat games. Initially developed mobile titles before transitioning to PC/console with Chorus (2021).

nodes.name: Focus Entertainment
nodes.summary: French video game publisher focused on AA and niche indie titles. Known for A Plague Tale, Evil West, Atomic Heart, and the Surge and GreedFall series.

nodes.name: Frogwares
nodes.summary: Ukrainian game developer — surviving and releasing games through war. Based in Kyiv (80 employees) with Dublin subsidiary. Best known for the Sherlock Holmes series (7M copies) and The Sinking City. Founded in 2000 by French expatriates. CEO Waël Amr.

nodes.name: FromSoftware
nodes.ownership: Kadokawa Corporation 69.66% (majority), Sony Interactive Entertainment 14.09%, Tencent (Sixjoy HK) 16.25%
nodes.summary: Renowned Japanese game developer; creators of Elden Ring, Dark Souls, Bloodborne. Headquartered in Shinjuku, Tokyo. President Hidetaka Miyazaki since 2014. Founded 1986, entered games 1994. Acquired by Kadokawa in 2014.

nodes.name: Frontier Developments plc
nodes.summary: British video game developer and publisher based in Cambridge, England, founded by David Braben. Known for the Elite Dangerous space sim, Planet Coaster/Zoo tycoon sims, F1 Manager series, and Jurassic World Evolution.
wikilinks: events/2023-10-17 — Frontier Developments organisational review redundancies

nodes.name: Gearbox Entertainment
nodes.summary: Gearbox Entertainment is a Texas-based video game developer and publisher best known for the Borderlands franchise. It was acquired by Embracer Group in April 2021 for up to $1.3 billion. nodes.name: Ghost Ship Games
nodes.summary: Danish video game developer based in Copenhagen. Best known for Deep Rock Galactic (2020), a cooperative first-person shooter featuring procedurally generated caves and dwarven miners. Created by a team with experience from IO Interactive, IO Interactive, and other Danish studios.

nodes.name: Google
nodes.ownership: Public (NASDAQ: GOOGL); subsidiary of Alphabet Inc.
nodes.summary: Gaming at Google consists primarily of the failed Stadia cloud gaming platform. HQ: Mountain View, CA.

nodes.name: Grasshopper Manufacture
nodes.summary: Japanese video game developer; cult-favorite action game studio known for the No More Heroes series. Founded in 1998 by Goichi Suda ("Suda51"). Headquartered in Tokyo. Acquired by NetEase in 2021.

nodes.name: Guerrilla Games
nodes.summary: Guerrilla Games is an Amsterdam-based AAA game developer and subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment. Best known for the Killzone series and, more recently, the Horizon franchise which has become a major pillar of Sony's first-party output.

nodes.name: Halo Studios
nodes.ownership: First-party subsidiary of Microsoft Gaming (Xbox Game Studios)
nodes.summary: Formerly 343 Industries. First-party Xbox studio founded in 2007 to manage the Halo franchise after Bungie's departure. HQ Redmond, WA. Rebranded to Halo Studios in October 2024 as part of a strategic reset.

nodes.name: Haveli Investments
nodes.summary: Austin, TX PE firm with a dedicated Gaming Fund. Co-acquirer of Jagex (2024, with CVC).

nodes.name: Haven Studios
nodes.ownership: Subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment (acquired March 2022)
nodes.summary: Montreal-based game developer and wholly-owned subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment. Founded in March 2021 by industry veteran Jade Raymond (former Ubisoft Toronto founder, EA Motive founder, Google Stadia VP).

nodes.name: Hello Games
nodes.summary: British video game developer and publisher based in Guildford, Surrey. Privately held, founder-owned. Best known for the Joe Danger series and No Man's Sky.

nodes.name: High Moon Studios
nodes.summary: San Diego-based Activision studio focused on Call of Duty support. Founded as Sammy Studios in 2002, acquired by Vivendi Games in 2006 and renamed High Moon Studios. After the Activision Blizzard merger, the studio was integrated into Activision's Call of Duty development pipeline.

nodes.name: HoYoverse (miHoYo)
nodes.region: CN (Shanghai) + SG (global publishing); offices in Montreal, LA, Tokyo, Seoul
nodes.summary: Chinese video game developer and publisher, HQ Shanghai. Best known for Genshin Impact, Honkai series, and Zenless Zone Zero. Private company (founder-owned), no public listing. Global publishing brand HoYoverse (Cognosphere Pte. Ltd.) based in Singapore since 2022.

nodes.name: IO Interactive
nodes.summary: Danish video game developer and publisher based in Copenhagen. Best known for the Hitman series (World of Assassination trilogy), Kane & Lynch, and the 2026 James Bond game 007 First Light.

nodes.name: Infinity Ward
nodes.region: US (Los Angeles, CA + Woodland Hills, CA)
nodes.summary: Original Call of Duty developer, best known for the Modern Warfare series. Founded in 2002 by Vince Zampella, Jason West, and Grant Collier. Acquired by Activision in 2003 after the breakout success of the original Call of Duty. The studio has approximately 500 employees.

nodes.name: Insomniac Games
nodes.summary: Insomniac Games is a Burbank, CA-based AAA game developer and subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment. Best known for the Spyro, Ratchet & Clank, and Marvel's Spider-Man series. Acquired by Sony in 2019, the studio operates dual locations (Burbank, CA and Durham, NC).

nodes.name: Jagex
nodes.summary: UK game studio (Cambridge), HQ. RuneScape publisher. Acquired 2024-02-09 by CVC Capital Partners + Haveli Investments (previously Carlyle, 2021).

nodes.summary: Former first-party Sony Interactive Entertainment studio based in Tokyo; historically Sony's home market development arm. Successor studio is orgs/Team Asobi.

nodes.name: Kadokawa Corporation

nodes.summary: Japan's largest media conglomerate; parent of FromSoftware, Spike Chunsoft, Acquire. Founded 1945 as Kadokawa Shoten (publishing), merged with Dwango (Niconico video platform) in 2014.

nodes.name: Keywords Studios
nodes.summary: Global gaming services provider (localization, audio, QA, development). UK-HQ, with US/CA staff. Acquired 2024-10-24 by the EQT + CPP + Temasek consortium ($2.8B).

nodes.name: King
nodes.ownership: Subsidiary of Activision Blizzard (→ Microsoft Gaming / Xbox, since Oct 2023)
nodes.summary: Swedish mobile game giant — creator of Candy Crush Saga (2012), one of the most successful free-to-play games of all time. 2,000 employees across 10 studios/offices. HQ Stockholm + London.

nodes.name: Koei Tecmo
nodes.summary: Japanese video game publisher and developer; creators of Dynasty Warriors, Ninja Gaiden, and Nioh. Formed in 2009 through the merger of Koei (founded 1978) and Tecmo (founded 1967). Headquartered in Yokohama. Known for the "musou" (warriors) genre of large-scale historical action games.

nodes.name: Konvoy Ventures
nodes.summary: Thesis-driven VC based in Denver, specializing in platforms and technologies at the frontier of gaming and interactive entertainment. Manages $270M across three funds. Best known for publishing the annual Games VC Report, a widely-cited industry report on games investment trends, M&A, and fundraising.

nodes.name: Kowloon Nights
nodes.summary: Video gaming investment fund established in 2017. Unlike traditional VC, provides project-based funding to talented teams for PC and console premium games. Takes a hands-off approach during development, empowering creative teams while providing financial support.

nodes.name: Krafton Inc.
nodes.summary: Krafton Inc. (stylized KRAFTON) is a South Korean video game holding company and publisher headquartered in Seongnam, South Korea. nodes.name: Larian Studios
nodes.ownership: Private (founder-owned, Swen Vincke majority owner; Tencent minority stake)
nodes.summary: Belgian independent AAA RPG developer — the Baldur's Gate 3 success story. Founded 1996 by Swen Vincke. Private company majority-owned by Vincke and his wife. Tencent holds a minority non-controlling stake. 530 employees across 7 global studios.

nodes.name: Lilith Games
nodes.summary: Lilith Games is a Chinese mobile game developer and publisher founded in 2013 by Wang Xinwen. The company is known for hit mobile titles including AFK Arena, Dislyte, Farlight 84, and Rise of Kingdoms. Lilith is one of China's most valuable private game companies (unicorn, valued at $22 billion RMB as of 2024).

nodes.name: London Venture Partners
nodes.summary: Seed-stage VC exclusively focused on the video games industry. Widely recognized as one of the most successful seed investors in gaming history — portfolio companies have created approximately $18-30 billion in combined value.

nodes.name: MachineGames
nodes.summary: Swedish first-person action developer, founded 2009. HQ Uppsala with a Sundsvall office. Acquired by ZeniMax Media in 2010. Known for revitalizing the Wolfenstein franchise and developing Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.

nodes.name: March Capital
nodes.summary: Venture growth firm headquartered in Santa Monica, California. Invests globally since 2014. Over $1.65B across four funds. Primary focus is AI-enabled enterprise software, but has notable gaming track record.

nodes.name: Microsoft acquires Mojang.md
nodes.summary: Microsoft announced the acquisition of Mojang (Minecraft developer) for $2.5 billion on September 15, 2014, closing November 6, 2014. Markus "Notch" Persson, the creator of Minecraft, left the company. Microsoft has continued to expand Minecraft across all platforms including PlayStation and Nintendo.

nodes.name: 2025 — No Man's Sky turnaround.md
nodes.summary: Hello Games' No Man's Sky launched August 9, 2016 to massive hype followed by disastrous reception. Missing features, server issues, and what was perceived as misleading marketing led to review bombs and refunds. Hello Games founder Sean Murray was criticized for promising features that didn't ship.

nodes.name: Nintendo Switch launches worldwide
nodes.summary: Nintendo's seventh major home console (hybrid handheld/home system). Launched globally on March 3, 2017 at $299.99 USD, following a January 2017 reveal event.

nodes.name: IO Interactive independence.md
nodes.summary: IO Interactive, the Danish developer of the Hitman series, completed a management buyout from Square Enix in June 2017. Square Enix had announced in May 2017 that it was divesting the studio due to disappointing financial results. IO Interactive retained the Hitman IP — a rare outcome in publisher-studio splits.

nodes.name: Microsoft acquires Compulsion Games
nodes.summary: At E3 2018 on June 10, 2018, Xbox head Phil Spencer announced that Microsoft had acquired Compulsion Games, making it part of Microsoft Studios (now Xbox Game Studios). The announcement was made alongside acquisitions of Ninja Theory, Playground Games, and Undead Labs as part of a major first-party studio expansion.

nodes.name: Microsoft acquires Obsidian Entertainment
nodes.summary: At X018 on November 10, 2018, Microsoft announced the acquisition of Obsidian Entertainment, bringing the veteran RPG developer into Xbox Game Studios. Obsidian, founded in 2003 by former Black Isle Studios staff, was known for Fallout: New Vegas, South Park: The Stick of Truth, and Pillars of Eternity.

nodes.name: Microsoft acquires inXile Entertainment
nodes.summary: At X018 on November 10, 2018, Microsoft announced the acquisition of inXile Entertainment alongside Obsidian Entertainment. inXile, founded by Brian Fargo in 2002, was known for the Wasteland series, Torment: Tides of Numenera, and The Bard's Tale IV.

nodes.name: DayZ standalone struggles.md
nodes.summary: DayZ, originally a mod for Arma 2, became a standalone survival game developed by Bohemia Interactive. Released in Early Access in December 2013. The game's development was prolonged and controversial, with a split between creator Dean Hall (who left in 2014) and Bohemia.

nodes.name: 4A Games Metro Exodus launch.md
nodes.summary: 4A Games released Metro Exodus on February 15, 2019 — the third entry in the Metro series. The game was a critical and commercial success. The studio, co-founded by veterans of the original Metro 2033 game, operates from both Kyiv, Ukraine and Sliema, Malta.

nodes.summary: At E3 2019 on June 9, 2019, Microsoft announced the acquisition of Double Fine Productions, the San Francisco-based studio founded by Tim Schafer in 2000. nodes.id: events/2020-03 — Warhorse Studios Kingdom Come success
nodes.name: Warhorse Studios Kingdom Come success.md
nodes.summary: Warhorse Studios' Kingdom Come: Deliverance, a historically accurate medieval RPG, launched February 13, 2018. Despite mixed reception on difficulty and pacing, it sold 6M+ copies by 2024, making it one of the most successful Czech games ever. A sequel, Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, was announced in April 2024 for early 2025 release.
